meta.title: Goods bed cost model v6 — worked numbers, fair-wage community state + investment layer
meta.source_doc: Deep OCR of canvas + Bunnings + INV-1507 invoices + Coastal Fasteners + Notion BK + v6 worked-numbers brief
v6_changes_2026_05_29: Community state now pays a FAIR WAGE: community labour $130/bed (band $100-$160) instead of $0 volunteer. Plastic stays $0 (community-collected, free).
Community DIRECT 140.74 -> 270.74 (band 240.74-300.74). Reframed from 'cheapest/vision' to 'economic PARITY with the factory ($275.74), margin stays community-owned'.

Community margin at $750 = $479.26 (64%); at institutional $801 = $530.26 (66%). Community state-5 ($270.74) is ~$5 BELOW the factory ($275.74); only at the top of the labour band (+$160) is it ~$25 more (the dignified-work premium).

Investment layer slotted in (UNVERIFIED/INFERRED): standalone_site_capex (3-site), volume_ramp_v6, demand_mix, margin_waterfall (brokerage/co-op split), debt_service, sensitivity_v6 (incl. 3-way joint downside + brokerage flex floor).
Confidence: community direct + v6 figures INFERRED (from a verified BOM); per-site capex UNVERIFIED (needs vendor quotes); Centrecorp $801 + BOM VERIFIED.

physics._hdpe_split_note: TWO QUANTITIES, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE (Ben ruling 2026-07-25, Matt model input 1). `hdpe_kg_per_bed` is the PURCHASED mass and is the costing basis: 20kg x $2.75/kg landed = $55/bed (Defy INV-1731, $2/kg shred + $0.75/kg delivery). `hdpe_in_product_kg_per_bed` is the mass in a FINISHED bed and is the only basis for the public diversion claim (mirrored by PLASTIC_KG_PER_BED in products.ts, which feeds CANONICAL_ASSETS.plasticKg). In Matt's workbook these are the cells `hdpe_purchased_kg_per_bed` and `hdpe_in_product_kg_per_bed`. Equal today ONLY because press yield has never been measured; item 6's instrumented run may separate them. Offcut is reshredded rather than landfilled, so purchased >= in-product always. Never collapse them: moving the costing mass would silently restate a public claim.

site_production_block._what_this_is: What BED SALES ALONE should carry at a community site, per year. Added 2026-07-25 (Matt model input 5). Before this, the entire site cost model was one line: LOCATIONS.on_country.rentPerYear = $24,000. That $24,000 is a CORRECT RENT FIGURE THAT WAS READ AS AN OPERATING COST, and dividing it into contribution is what produced the '75 to 100 beds a year' claim that ruling I retired.
site_production_block._why_not_the_dewr_headline: The Oonchiumpa REAL Innovation Fund Stage Two application gives a bare facility at ~$151,666/yr and a fully staffed one at ~$341,666/yr. Dividing contribution into those gives 447 and 1,007 beds/yr, and BOTH ARE WRONG IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION to the $24,000: they make bed sales carry the program's share of rent, insurance and admin, which two-pots forbids. The DEWR budget funds a facility AND a youth employment program in one building. The honest number is a third one, split at the line level below.
site_production_block._three_pots: 1) NETWORK BLOCK (~$109,500/yr, the engine's existing `fixedBlock` less location rent: design, quality, training, back office, field travel). Amortises across sites; this is what Goods. is for after a handover. NOTE the DEWR budget already pays INTO this: its 'ACT: community-owned machinery plus Trainer / WHS' line, $63,333/yr, is REVENUE to Goods., not a cost to it, and no model currently shows that. 2) SITE PRODUCTION BLOCK (this object). Carried by bed sales. 3) SITE WRAPAROUND BLOCK ($300,000/yr employment brokerage plus the program share of the lines below). Grant funded by design, and it must never touch per-bed economics on paper.

dewr_lines.basis: The plant exists to make product. No program use.
Anchored on the engine's own rent lines: a production shed On Country reads $24K to $30K. The balance is the office, training room and services the program needs.
Production carries plant, public liability, product liability and workers comp on the production crew. The program adds participant and volunteer cover at a higher premium than a manufacturing crew.
Invoicing, BAS, inventory and board reporting are production. Grant acquittal, DEWR compliance reporting and participant data are program.

site_production_block._supervisor_is_an_open_decision: OPEN, Ben and Nic (Matt model input 5). The DEWR $150,000 Project Manager is a REAL Innovation Fund PROGRAM role, not a production supervisor. Production needs a working line supervisor for quality, materials ordering, scheduling and WHS on the press, and that role is in NEITHER model. The costs below are ASSUMED, not costed roles. Default is `none` deliberately: it is the computed floor and the only option that assumes no undecided role. Do not treat any single row as the answer; the honest denominator is the BAND.
site_production_block._do_not_double_count: The community path already carries $130/bed fair-wage production labour inside its marginal cost. A supervisor sits ON TOP of that, not inside it.
site_production_block._contribution_correction: Every break-even published before 2026-07-25 divided into $329.26, which is the community path at the SYDNEY location where inbound freight is $0. That is the wrong location for a community site. On Country carries $60/bed inbound freight, and the engine subtracts $70/bed when containerised (ship the plant to the feedstock once, rather than shipping finished beds out N times). Intended shape, On Country containerised: marginal $410.74, contribution $339.26, which is slightly BETTER than what was published. On Country NOT containerised: marginal $480.74, contribution $269.26, which is materially worse and is the case that breaks things.
site_production_block._the_answer: The honest denominator is 234 to 529 beds a year (bare 234, half-time supervisor 381, full-time 529, all at $339.26 contribution). Where it lands inside that band is decided by one unresolved question: who pays the person who runs the line. Compare: the retired $24,000 rent basis gave 71.
site_production_block._fragility_is_the_useful_part: At Matt's deliberately conservative 500 beds/yr against a ~$105,000 replication plant, three dials each flip the answer on their own. Drop to 250/yr and the site cannot cover its own production block at all. Do not containerise and 2.6 years becomes 19.8. Make the supervisor full-time and it never retires the plant. So the honest read is NOT 'a community site pays off its plant in under three years'. It is that there is a plausible configuration where production alone retires the plant in a few years, and three things we have not measured or decided each decide whether that is real.
site_production_block._claims_status: DEWR figures are AS WRITTEN in the REAL Innovation Fund Stage Two application. The production/program splits are DERIVED here and are assumptions, not stated figures; they are the thing to argue with. Supervisor costs are ASSUMED, not costed roles. Break-evens are ARITHMETIC off those inputs and off a contribution figure that is itself MODELLED from a run whose per-bed actuals were never captured (Matt model input 6). Nothing here is measured. No figure here goes on a slide, in an email, or into a community meeting as a headline.

capex_modules._what_this_is: A BASKET OF MODULES a community selects from, replacing the build_method LADDER for the purpose of pricing a real pathway. Added 2026-07-25 (Matt model input 7, created by ruling D: the object is INFRASTRUCTURE, not 'a plant'). `build_states` remains the ladder and is untouched, because its outputs are published; this is the additive structure that can price a subset.
capex_modules._the_defect_this_fixes: Every `build_method` value assumes a WHOLE SITE built in one fixed order, and each `capital_added` is a rung on that ladder. Against the four live pathways the ladder prices exactly one: Oonchiumpa (a full facility). It cannot price Utopia (wants a shredder: no configuration is collection-and-shredding without pressing), Tennant Creek (wants to work through an existing shed: site capex and rent are assumed, not supplied by the partner) or Palm Island (wants to start with governance: no configuration has zero plant and a real cost). Three of four.
capex_modules._site_base_is_not_a_module: The honest structure is SITE BASE + MODULES, not modules alone. Utopia wanting 'a shredder' still needs power, a pad and somewhere to put it. Where a partner supplies the shed, as at Tennant Creek, the base shrinks instead of vanishing, and by how much is a question for that partner, not a number we can assert.
capex_modules._source_and_grades: Capex bands come from the replication table in `2026-07-22-minimal-viable-facility-model.md` (market rates for a NEW site, which are honestly higher than what Nic paid second hand). Grades are per line: `evidenced` from a Xero bill, `ben` from Ben's market figures, `estimate` at Australian market rates, `unpriced` where no figure exists yet. Reassembling these into modules is an ALLOCATION of an evidenced total, not new evidence.

site_base.label: Site base (required by any production module)
site_base._partner_supplied_note: Where a partner supplies the shed, power or pad, subtract those lines rather than the whole base. Tennant Creek is the live case and the subtraction has not been agreed with them.

modules.label: Collection and baling
modules._note: NOT in the MVF replication table and genuinely unpriced: bins, bags, a baler, local transport. This is a real gap, not an oversight in the table. It is upstream of the shredder, so it is load-bearing for Utopia, which is the pathway asking for the earliest module. Needs a quote before Utopia can be priced.

modules.label: Shredding
modules._note: Telford Smith. Physically confirmed and running; the invoice is not in the connected Xero, which is the outstanding paperwork on ruling O. Priced as a single unit, so no allocation is involved.

modules.label: Pressing, CNC and finishing
modules._note: Circularity Group INV-0054 covers hot press, cold press AND CNC as ONE bill, so pressing and CNC CANNOT be split from evidence. Deliberately left bundled rather than split on a guessed ratio. NO live pathway currently needs them separate: Utopia stops at shredding, Tennant Creek is a shed question, Palm Island has no plant. Split it when a vendor breakdown exists and a pathway actually requires it.

modules.label: Assembly and workshop
modules._note: Carbatec Brisbane, two bills. Tagged ACT-HV Harvest in Xero rather than ACT-GD, which is a tagging problem, not a doubt about the spend.

modules.label: Sales and delivery
modules._note: No capex. Freight already sits in the engine per bed (inbound freight by location, long-haul, and the containerise delta).

capex_modules._operating_allocation_is_not_done: The $79,333 bare site production block in `site_production_block` assumes the FULL module set. A subset carries less, and the per-module split of machine upkeep, rent share, insurance and admin has NOT been derived. Until it is, do not quote an operating figure for a partial pathway. This is the next piece of work on item 7 and it is why the pathway entries below carry capex only.

live_pathways.label: Oonchiumpa: a full facility
live_pathways.priceable: partly, blocked only on collection_baling being unpriced
live_pathways._note: The only pathway the old ladder could price, and even it assumed collection came free.

live_pathways.label: Utopia: a shredder
live_pathways._note: Utopia's own answer to 'what would you want to own first' was a shredder. That answer is worth more than any figure in the model, and the ladder could not price it at all.

live_pathways.label: Tennant Creek: work through an existing shed
live_pathways.priceable: no, the base subtraction is not agreed with the partner
live_pathways._note: The module capex is knowable; what the partner supplies is not, and it is their call, not ours.

live_pathways.label: Palm Island: start with governance
live_pathways.priceable: no, and this is the honest answer
live_pathways._note: Zero plant and a REAL cost. A model that prices this at $0 is wrong in a way that matters, because governance work is the most common first step and the most consistently unfunded. Needs a governance/scoping cost line that is not plant.

capex_modules._claims_status: PROPOSED STRUCTURE, not agreed as a workbook shape. Capex bands are reassembled from evidenced and estimated MVF lines; the reassembly is an allocation. Collection and baling is genuinely unpriced. Per-module operating shares are NOT derived. No figure here is a quote.

canonical_bom._note: Mirrors supplier-quotes.ts. Defy-kit path direct materials = $469.79/bed.

steel_poles.source: DNA Steel Direct (Alice Springs, in Notion)

_capital_added_note: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY `capital_added` VALUE. These are RUNGS ON ONE LADDER, not four site configurations. Each `capital_added` is the INCREMENT over the previous state; `capital_cumulative` is the running total ($2,000 / $38,000 / $160,000 / $30,000, cumulative $230,000). The community state's $30,000 means 'having already built the ~$200,000 central factory, adding the community configuration costs $30,000 more'. It has NEVER meant 'a community site costs $30,000', and quoting it that way is a category error, not a rounding difference (retired as a site price, Ben ruling 2026-07-25, Matt model input 2). Sunk spend on the existing farm facility is ALREADY_INVESTED ($110,046, actual). A fresh site's gross build cost is the rough and variable $112,000-$222,000 range, plausibly reaching about $200,000. Structural fix pending: capex should become a basket of modules a community selects from (collection/baling, shredding, pressing, CNC/finishing, assembly, sales/delivery), because a ladder cannot price Utopia (a shredder only), Tennant Creek (an existing shed) or Palm Island (governance first).

state_2_defy_kits.label: Defy Kits (buy cut+finished kits, assemble in-house)
state_2_defy_kits._note: Fastest path. Best for ramping while facility being set up.

state_3_defy_panels.label: Defy Panels (buy panels, CNC + assemble)
state_3_defy_panels._note: Worst value — paying for panels we could press ourselves. Only use if press is broken.

state_4_factory.label: Factory (raw shred → press → CNC → assemble in-house)
state_4_factory._note: TARGET state + PARITY COMPARATOR for the community state. $474.26 margin at $750 retail (63%). 4 beds/day × 250 working days = 1,000/yr from one facility. The community state ($270.74) sits ~$5 below this — fair-wage community production is economically on par with the centralised factory.

state_5_community.label: Community (waste plastic free, fair-wage paid work)
state_5_community._note: ECONOMIC PARITY with the factory ($275.74) — not the cheap state. At $270.74 it is ~$5 BELOW the factory; only at the top of the labour band (+$160) is it ~$25 more (the dignified-work premium). $479.26 margin at $750 (64%) / $530.26 at $801 (66%). The margin stays community-owned AND the build is dignified paid work, not free volunteer labour.

first_principles_floor._principle: Musk Idiot Index: what's the absolute minimum a bed could cost if every input was bought at raw-market rate and assembled at industry-low labour rates?

components.source: Coastal Fasteners verified + bulk bolt estimate

first_principles_floor._implication: $340.80/bed of supply-chain markup we could capture in-house at scale. That's the capital-investment case.

idiot_index.markup_pays_for: Shredding + pressing + CNC + finishing + Defy margin. BIGGEST LEVERAGE — moves $304/bed if we shred + press + CNC in-house.
Hot-press + Defy margin. Panel-path is the WORST value — buy raw shred or buy finished kits, not panels.
Cut to length + drill + Alice Springs delivery. Already reasonable.
Cut + hem + grommet + sew + sewist labour. Centre Canvas is competitive against raw 12oz cotton at $62/m self-cut ($130/bed).
At-cost from Coastal Fasteners — already raw rate.
Already competitive — Defy assembly is reasonable vs in-house $40-$80.

counterfactual.source: Retail furniture / contract supply mid-2026 AU market scan

capex_required_to_reach_state_4._capital_ask_basis: GROSS capex to reach Factory state. Net ask ~1,954 (low) / ~111,954 (high) after the 110,046 already invested (facility 100,000 + Carbatec tooling 10,046).

qbe_pitch_inputs._principle: QBE standard funder pitch: Capital ask + unit economics + scaling plan. Sliders should expose these levers.
qbe_pitch_inputs._capital_ask_basis: GROSS capex; net ~1,954 / ~111,954 after the 110,046 already invested.
qbe_pitch_inputs.headline_value_per_dollar_at_target: Each $1,000 of capital invested unlocks ~$X/bed cost reduction, ~Y beds/yr capacity

standalone_site_capex._note: v6: a community/standalone site is a smaller plant than the central factory. Three sites modelled. UNVERIFIED — needs vendor quotes. vs v5 single factory $112-222K → ~1.5-2x for 3 distributed sites.

volume_ramp_v6._note: v6 3-site ramp. Per-site capacity 250/yr is a MODELLING ASSUMPTION (flag — not a verified throughput).

demand_mix._note: v6 demand segmentation. Institutional anchor VERIFIED (Centrecorp INV-0291, 107 beds @ $85,712 = $801/bed). Retail/corp-RAP gift price is the BIGGEST UNKNOWN. Community/humanitarian subsidised.

segments.label: Retail / corporate-RAP gift
segments._flag: biggest unknown — no firm retail/RAP price anchor yet

margin_waterfall._note: v6 per-bed waterfall at institutional $801, COMMUNITY production ($270.74 COGS). Splits the landed margin into ACT brokerage (debt service), a cashflow buffer, and the community co-op margin. The act_brokerage slider MUST FLEX (see sensitivity_v6 joint downside).

debt_service._note: v6 debt-service coverage off the ACT brokerage slice. Base 200/bed brokerage on ~480 revenue beds/yr ≈ $96,000/yr. A thin 60/bed UNDER-covers the $500K matching tranche; the brokerage FLOOR if carrying the full $500K is ~$91/bed (>=$35,000/384).
debt_service.brokerage_floor_basis: >=35000/384 ≈ 91/bed if carrying the full 500K matching tranche

sensitivity_v6._note: v6 ±20% sensitivity dials + two load-bearing insights. (1) The Defy HDPE kit dial has ZERO effect on the community state (free collected plastic decouples it from Defy pricing). (2) The 3-way JOINT DOWNSIDE is the load-bearing CDFI/equity design point.
sensitivity_v6._defy_kit_decoupled_reason: community state uses free community-collected plastic, so its COGS is independent of the Defy HDPE kit price.

joint_downside.implication: Under the joint downside the community co-op margin collapses to ~$14/bed while ACT debt is still serviced. Therefore the act_brokerage slider MUST FLEX DOWN in a downside (step to ~100/bed when margin/bed falls below a floor) or it crushes the community. This flex is the key CDFI/equity design point.
